html:
Performers
Carol Brice (contralto), Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Fritz Reiner (conductor) Documented

Carol Brice is credited only on sides 1, 4 and 6. Individual orchestral players are not identified.

[1] [3]
Work version
The ballet in thirteen numbers, recorded on six 78-rpm sides Inferred, not documented

The thirteen numbers are listed side by side on the Columbia set and match the number sequence of the ballet version; the performing edition used by the orchestra is unknown.

[1] [3] [5]
Recorded
1946-02-05 Documented

Both the Internet Archive item and Sony’s box-set notes give 5 February 1946. The same notes record other sessions of 2 and 4 February 1946 for other works.

[1] [3]
Place
Syria Mosque, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania Documented

The Pittsburgh Symphony’s regular recording venue in these sessions.

[1] [3]
Label
Columbia Masterworks Documented

78-rpm album set; the set was reissued on a ten-inch LP, ML 2006, in 1948.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
M-633 (78s 12409-D to 12411-D); automatic sequence MM-633 (12412-D to 12414-D) Documented

The Internet Archive item is labelled MM-633.

[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Six sides, matrices XCO 35816 (Nos. 1–⁠3), 35817 (Nos. 4–⁠6), 35818 (Nos. 7–⁠8), 35819 (Nos. 9–⁠10), 35820 (No. 11), 35821 (Nos. 12–⁠13); take 1 Documented

The Internet Archive item and Sony’s notes give the same matrix numbers and side contents.

[1] [3]
Transfer
Shellackophile collection, Internet Archive Documented

The item sits in the Internet Archive’s shellackophile-recordings collection; no personal mastering credit is given.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was uploaded on 1 April 2022; the date of the transfer itself is not stated.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

Equipment, equalisation and restoration settings are not stated. The file is a single continuous MP3 of the six sides.

[1]
Composition rights
Falla died on 14 November 1946. Spanish law protects the works of authors who died before 7 December 1987 for life plus 80 years, so his music remains protected in Spain until the end of 2026; arrangements and modern editions carry their own rights Documented

A phonogram term assessment does not clear the composition, an arrangement or a modern score edition.

[7] [8]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1947, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applied to a Columbia set issued in 1947 (the Internet Archive item says March 1947, Sony’s notes 24 February 1947, Discogs 1947). This is a territorial phonogram basis, not US or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

[1] [3] [4]

Falla, El amor brujo; Carol Brice, contralto; Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra; Fritz Reiner. Columbia Masterworks M-633/MM-633 (1947 issue), Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Falla’s composition remains protected in Spain until the end of 2026.
